attempts.summary: Here is the paragraph to save in that file: The decoder findings held in this data: a position decoder trained on rewarded laps failed once licking stopped after reward removal, and its error rose along the whole track. The place-field findings held only in part: reliability fell without reward, but field counts, widths, out-of-field firing and field turnover did not match, probably because the paper does not describe how it computed dF/F and fields from raw fluorescence. The dopamine inhibition results held in direction but not in the saline control. The dopamine axon imaging and time controls are missing from the dataset, so those findings could not be tested. Figures 2 and 3 rest on only 2 mice, so the place-field results are weak evidence either way.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Krishnan, Heer, Cherian and Sheffield (2022) on dandiset 000462, which holds suite2p fluorescence and behaviour of 10 wild-type mice in the reward extinction task and 4 DAT-Cre mice with VTA DREADD inhibition. It decodes position from CA1 activity across rewarded, unrewarded and re-rewarded laps, defines place fields and their parameters, and compares them after DCZ, CNO and saline. The control mice, pupil data and VTA axon imaging are not in the dandiset.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds 10 of the 12 wild-type extinction mice and 4 of the 6 DREADD mice, and none of the time-control mice, dark sessions, pupil recordings, tdTomato control mice or VTA axon imaging. Nine of the 41 claims cannot be tested for this reason, and the dark part of a tenth.

sub-014 has 129000 behaviour rows for 135000 fluorescence frames. Decoding position from the fluorescence shows the behaviour matches with no shift up to frame 71000 and matches 6000 frames later fluorescence from there on, so 6000 behaviour rows are missing at the start of BeforeCNO and every later row is misaligned in the file. sub-NR6 has 8 extra behaviour rows and sub-CFC4 one row fewer, at the end.

Conditions are given only as frame counts in the free-text description of the fluorescence series (for example 'Rewarded 15000, Unrewarded 20000', written with colons); there are no epochs or trial tables. The behaviour channels have no units ('behavior'); position is in volts with no scale to cm, and reward and lick are voltage traces.

The DREADD files' raw fluorescence carries a constant offset of about 16400 to 17000 counts (file minima 16415 to 16471) that the wild-type files do not have (minima 57 to 678) and the description does not mention; dF/F computed without removing it is 8.0 to 12.1 times too small (99th percentile over the first 9000 frames of 40 cells per file).

The files hold raw suite2p fluorescence only, without neuropil, dF/F, transients or the place cells the paper used, and the subjects carry no label for the mice in each figure (for example the 3 mice of Figures 2 and 3).

The ImagingPlane indicator is given as 'GFP' while the description says GCaMP6f, every file has the same session_start_time (2021-12-13T02:30:00-06:00) and age P12W, and the DREADD files' session description reads 'Reward expectation extinction' for four days of recordings.

Question for the authors - how was dF/F computed from the suite2p traces (baseline window and percentile, neuropil), and what rule defined a significant transient and a candidate place field (refs. 44, 67 and 75 are cited)? This attempt used the 8th percentile in a 15 s window, transients from 2 to 0.5 SD of at least 0.5 s, and bins above 25% of the way from baseline to peak; its fields are wider than the paper's (70 to 90 cm against 53 cm in R); the candidate regions it cuts (per-mouse means 31.4 to 43.2 cm) are narrower than the paper's fields (53 to 61 cm), and the Methods width rule widens them to 61 to 86 cm.

Question for the authors - how is lap time defined, and how is the position voltage converted to cm? The behaviour clock agrees with the 1.5 s reward pause (46 to 49 frames at 30 Hz) and the wild-type mice run 4.11 R laps per minute, yet the time from 0 to 200 cm is 12.2 s per R lap (8.5 s counting running frames only) against the paper's 7.34 s, and DREADD lap speeds are about 26 cm/s against 42.

Question for the authors - over which frames is the approach ratio computed, and is velocity normalised as in define_attentivelaps.py? Over the traversal (lap start to the track end) the Methods ratio is 2.21 in R and 1.75 in UR and 46% of RE low laps are engaged; over the whole lap with the reward pause many laps have no defined ratio; the code's normalised ratio over the traversal gives 1.26, 1.20 and 67%, the closest to the reported 1.3, 1.22 and 70%.
Question for the authors - what defines a reward cell (ref. 24) - what counts as firing in the 40 cm reward zone and within 2 s (or 1.5 s, Supplementary Fig. 14a) of reward delivery?
Question for the authors - how were stable and remapped fields told apart in Figure 2e, and which mice and laps form Figures 2 and 3?

In 4 of the 10 extinction mice (NR6, NR14, NR23, CFC16) a reward is delivered in the Unrewarded condition as the description's frame counts delimit it: at the end of the first complete UR lap in NR6 and NR14, and in the partial lap that opens UR in NR23 and CFC16. Either the boundary is a little early or the reward was switched off a lap after imaging of UR began.

The paper's code keeps only part of some sessions (task_framestokeep in AnimalDetails/AnimalDetailsWT.py; for NR6 only the first 11100 of 20000 R frames) and changes some lick stops by hand (change_lick_stop); the paper does not mention either, and the dandiset holds the full sessions.

The Methods give pre-licking in UR as lasting '5 +/- 1' laps, but the same Methods count 90 RE high laps over 12 mice, 7.5 laps per mouse; and they say 4 of 12 mice licked randomly after the lick stop in one passage and that only one animal did in another.

entries.title: CA1 spatial maps after reward expectation extinction (Krishnan et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Krishnan, Heer, Cherian and Sheffield (2022) on dandiset 000462, which holds suite2p fluorescence and behaviour of 10 wild-type mice in the reward extinction task and 4 DAT-Cre mice with VTA DREADD inhibition. It decodes position from CA1 activity across rewarded, unrewarded and re-rewarded laps, defines place fields and their parameters, and compares them after DCZ, CNO and saline. The control mice, pupil data and VTA axon imaging are not in the dandiset.
